title: Backoff safety wrappers and idempotency migration path for SDKs
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem:
Teams integrating Redwood SDKs face inconsistent retry defaults, unclear idempotency semantics, and differing streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go. This causes production incidents where clients either retry too aggressively (amplifying load) or not enough (user-facing failures), and increases developer confusion when migrating between SDKs.

Goals:
- Provide opinionated and safe default retry/backoff policies for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that balance latency SLOs with amplification risk.
- Define clear idempotency key semantics and ergonomic helpers for common patterns (sync requests, async completions, streaming responses).
- Publish a small, actionable retryable error taxonomy that SDKs map to consistent behavior.
- Provide migration guidance and a compatibility shim for existing customers to opt into new defaults.

Non-goals:
- We will not change server-side retry semantics or API-level error codes.
- We will not implement distributed transactional semantics; idempotency here is at request-level.

Proposal (high level):
1) Default retry policy (opinionated across SDKs):
   - Retryable classes: transient_network, server_overload, transient_resource_exhaustion.
   - Default attempts: 3 total attempts (1 initial + 2 retries).
   - Backoff: jittered exponential with base=150ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=2s.
   - Rate-limit aware: if we see 429/RateLimit and response header X-RateLimit-Reset, respect Retry-After/Reset and cap retries to 1 after respect.

2) Idempotency primitives:
   - Automatic idempotency key generation for idempotent endpoints (create/completions-with-result) when caller does not supply one; key = sha256(project+user_id+canonical_payload + timestamp-truncated) with deterministic mode disabled by default.
   - Explicit idempotency API: call options.idempotency_key = "..." to control behavior.
   - Server response mapping: if server returns IdempotencyConflict, SDK surfaces IdempotencyConflictError (non-retryable) and provides the recorded-result link if present.

3) Streaming ergonomics:
   - Partial-delivery retries: streaming methods default to no automatic retries once any bytes have been flushed to user callback. For resumable streams (batchable generation with cursor) SDKs provide a ResumableStream helper: it tracks last-acked token offset and can request server resume from offset using an opaque resume_token when service supports it.
   - For short-lived client streams (single request, streaming response), provide an onError handler that receives the mapped taxonomy and a composed retry helper that only retries only if no payload was delivered to the user callback.

4) Error taxonomy (canonical):
   - transient_network: DNS failures, TCP resets, connection timeouts. -> safe to retry.
   - server_overload: 5xx with rate-shedding header, or 503/429 without idempotency side-effects. -> retry with backoff, but be conservative on retries.
   - transient_resource_exhaustion: OOM/worker-preempt signals from infra (mapped from specific 5xx codes). -> retryable but prefer fallback model variant.
   - client_4xx_non_retriable: invalid_request, bad_auth -> do not retry.
   - idempotency_conflict: server indicates duplicate operation already processed -> do not retry; return recorded result where available.

SDK-specific ergonomics (examples):
- Python (pseudocode):
  from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy
  client = Client(retry_policy=RetryPolicy.default())
  # default() implements the policy above and exposes .with_attempts() for override
  result = client.completions.create(prompt, idempotency_key=None)

- TypeScript (pseudocode):
  import { RedwoodClient, DefaultRetry } from '@redwood/sdk'
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ retry: DefaultRetry })
  // streaming: resume helper
  const stream = client.completions.stream(prompt)
  stream.on('data', (token) => console.log(token))
  stream.on('error', (err) => {
    if (DefaultRetry.isRetryable(err) && !stream.deliveredAny()) {
      await DefaultRetry.run(() => client.completions.create(prompt))
    }
  })

- Go (pseudocode):
  cli := redwood.NewClient(redwood.DefaultRetry())
  resp, err := cli.CreateCompletion(ctx, req)
  if err != nil { return err }

Compatibility/migration path:
- Provide a feature flag in SDK config: "compat.retries=v1" (legacy) | "v2" (new defaults). The default at release will be "v2" but customers can opt back to legacy for 2 months.
- A health-check tool in SDKs (redwood sdk-check) that runs a small matrix of calls to report whether their workload will be sensitive to new defaults (flags long-running or stateful APIs).

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose a RetryPolicy object with the documented defaults.
- Idempotency helpers implemented with consistent key format and server-mapping behavior across SDKs.
- Streaming helper library (ResumableStream) implemented in Python & TS (Go prioritized if time permits).
- Documentation published: developer guide, migration guide, and quickstart snippets for each language.
- E2E tests and chaos tests demonstrating retry behavior under intermittent failure patterns.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Generated idempotency keys must avoid embedding PII by default. Default generator uses project+user-id-hash + payload-hash truncated; we explicitly document how to opt-out.
- Security review required for idempotency key exposure patterns and resume-token handling.

Notes and references:
- Related tickets: ENG-31628 (cross-sdk semantics), ENG-20641 (retry guardrails).
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123 (TS), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4127 (Python).
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/Retry+and+Idempotency+2026

Decision log (short):
- 2026-03-02: Team agreed on 3 attempts and 150ms base after reviewing production latency profiles; trade-off: slightly higher latency tail vs fewer customer failures.
- 2026-03-05: Decided to default no-stream-retries after bytes flushed; provide resumable helper instead to avoid partial-duplicate outputs.
- 2026-03-09: Chosen to require security review for resume-token surface area.
acceptance_criteria: RetryPolicy.default() implemented in Python/TS/Go and wired into client initializers
Idempotency helper and explicit idempotency_key option implemented and tested
ResumableStream helper shipped for Python and TS with unit & integration tests
Migration docs and compat flag published to docs.redwood.com
E2E retry behavior validated via chaos tests and added to CI
